summary: Move module setup (AnsibleModule creation with argument_spec and constraints) out of main() into its own function so tests can check argument processing directly, as in the rds example.
questions: How do I test argument validation without running the whole module?
How should I structure main() to make my module testable?
How do I test that a required parameter is enforced?

answer_card.title: Split module setup out of main()
answer_card.answer_md:
Put module construction in its own function and keep `argument_spec` at module level:
```python
def setup_module_object():
    return AnsibleAWSModule(argument_spec=argument_spec,
                            required_if=required_if,
                            mutually_exclusive=[[...]])

def main():
    module = setup_module_object()
    validate_parameters(module)
    conn = setup_client(module)
    module.exit_json(**run_task(module, conn))
```
Then a test can call `set_module_args({...})` without the required `db_instance_identifier` and assert `AnsibleFailJson` is raised from the setup function. See `test/units/module_utils/aws/test_rds.py`.
